title: Mechanisms of Pneumococcal Persistence During Carriage
text:
RELEVANCE (See instructions):
The focus of this ongoing project is bacterial infection by a common respiratory pathogen, Streptococcus 
pneumoniae. The research program uses in vivo studies to define the mechanisms involved in the ability of 
this organism to cause disease, which follows colonization of its biological niche in the upper respiratory 
tract.

title: Computational imaging approaches to personalized gastric cancer treatment
text:
Gastric cancer (i.e., stomach cancer) is a major public health burden with a high incidence and
mortality worldwide. In this project, we propose to develop computational imaging approaches to the
prediction of treatment response and prognosis of gastric cancer. Success of our research may help
select the most effective treatment for an individual patient, which will not only improve outcomes for
patients in the US but also have global impact.

title: Advanced Course in Cancer Control Implementation Research
text:
Implementation research aims to shorten the translation gap from discovery to applying evidence-based
interventions in real-world community and clinical settings. The Advanced Course in Cancer Control
Implementation Research training program will provide researchers with advanced training in disparities-
focused implementation research for cancer control through a 4-day course offered annually and combined
with ongoing mentorship. This training for the next generation of cancer researchers will improve the adoption
of interventions and implementation strategies to help eliminate cancer disparities.

title: Causes and consequences of tRNA ligation defects in neurodegeneration
text:
This research proposes to investigate the basic molecular biological and biochemical mechanisms by which
aggregated proteins and dysregulated RNAs participate in the pathogenesis of neurodegeneration, a leading
cause of disability and suffering in the United States. In particular, we will study the link between protein
aggregation and altered tRNA processing in a large and growing family of genetic neurodegenerative diseases
without any therapies and that afflict both adults and children. If successful, the proposed research could
establish new, rationally targeted therapies in these and other neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Discovering Chemical Activity Networks-Predicting Bioactivity Based on Structure
text:
We encounter a wide diversity of chemicals throughout our lives, but we are not yet equipped to understand
which of these chemicals actually pose health risks. Furthermore, for the chemicals known to produce human
disease, we do not fully understand how they lead to adverse outcomes. This project will systematically
evaluate the toxicity of thousands of chemicals and discover the biological networks they modulate to help the
research and regulatory communities predict the toxicity of relevant chemicals.

title: Functional Interrogation of Human Acute Myeloid Leukemia Stem Cells
text:
Numerous studies have led to a model that human AML is driven by leukemia stem cells (LSCs). However, few
functional studies have been conducted in patient cells limiting the utility of this model for translational studies.
Our objectives are to use newly developed methods to interrogate important questions including the requirement
for specific mutations in disease initiation and maintenance, the dynamics of individual LSCs, and the effect of
targeted elimination of LSCs in AML progression.

title: Implementation of Continuum of Care Sepsis Phenotyping and Risk Stratification
text:
Sepsis is a common and costly syndrome causing 250,000 deaths/year in the USA and despite
much research, almost all new therapies have not helped patients survive longer. Artificial
intelligence may allow healthcare workers to identify and treat sepsis by using data available
from the electronic health record and has shown major promise to help combat sepsis. The goal
of my research is to become an expert who can use new technology to improve the care and
well-being of people who have sepsis.

title: Investigating the role of the mismatch repair proteins MSH2 and MSH6 in genome stability
text:
Mutations in the genes encoding the mismatch repair proteins MSH2 and MSH6 are associated with both
germline and spontaneous somatic cancers. MSH2-MSH6 has two distinct functions in genome stability: a
well-studied role to correct misincorporation errors made by the replicative polymerases, and an
underappreciated role to regulate the homologous recombination DNA repair pathway to prevent genome
rearrangements caused by exchange of genetic information between mismatched repeats. This proposal
seeks to fill the knowledge gap on the mechanism of regulation of homologous recombination by MSH2 and
MSH6 and its clinical significance.

title: Neuroinflammation and Neurogenesis in Schizophrenia
text:
Deep within the human brain lies a reservoir of stem cells capable of generating new
neurons throughout life. We will build a molecular map of all cell types within this reservoir,
which will allow us to understand how increased presence of immune cells in
schizophrenia support or hinder the development of new neurons. This work will bring us
closer to unlocking the potential of these stem cells to treat both psychiatric and
neurological brain diseases in the future.
.

title: Research Training - Biological Sciences
text:
The purpose of the Biological Sciences Training Program at Yale University is to train postdoctoral fellows,
including basic neuroscientists (PhD’s) and psychiatry residents (MD and/or MD/PhD’s) in biological and
behavioral sciences relevant to mental health. The overall objective is to promote cross-fertilization between
basic and clinical neuroscience researchers, so that trainees can go on to conduct translational research to
elucidate the molecular and cellular basis of complex behaviors. The training program is directly relevant to the
research mission of the NIMH because it fosters the education of researchers who will become dedicated to
the generation of new knowledge about maladaptive behavior related to major psychiatric illnesses and novel
treatment strategies.

title: Mobile Ecological Momentary Diet Assessment: A Low Burden, Ecologically-Valid Approach to Measuring Dietary Intake in Near-Real Time
text:
A dietary assessment approach that reduces participant and researcher burden and improves recall accuracy
and ecological validity is needed to move the field forward. In response, we propose to develop and test a low
cost mobile app that uses ecological momentary assessment to collect dietary data with limited burden and
notable accuracy. Our approach will be additionally unique from traditional dietary assessment approaches in
that it can be easily adapted for use as a dietary behavior change tool.

title: Spreading Tau Pathology in Non-Amnestic Alzheimer's Disease
text:
One influential theory of how Alzheimer’s disease spreads in the brain is that toxic tau is transported through
the brain’s white matter, along the axons of neurons; however, evidence for this model is incomplete. If axonal
transport is a common mechanism of tau spread, it should leave behind a signature of tau accumulation and
degeneration affecting the white matter networks that correspond to a patient’s primary cognitive symptoms.
We will combine longitudinal imaging of tau progression and white matter change with postmortem
histopathology to assess evidence for the axonal transport model in amnestic and non-amnestic variants of
Alzheimer’s disease that are known to affect distinct cognitive networks.

title: The Calm Bladder Study-A Phase 3 multicenter randomized controlled trial to evaluate acupuncture for the management of urinary symptoms in patients with NMIBC undergoing induction intravesical therapy
text:
Patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer commonly experience severe urinary symptoms secondary to
the cancer and the cancer treatments that can be associated with substantial decreases in quality of life and
delays in treatment or early discontinuation of effective adjuvant therapies. In a pilot study in patients undergoing
treatment for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, we demonstrated that patients could safely receive in-clinic
acupuncture prior to receiving intravesical bladder cancer therapies, with a reduction in their urinary symptoms.
We propose a large, definitive, multi-site trial to test the effectiveness of a standardized and scalable in-clinic
pre-procedure acupuncture intervention to improve urinary symptom burden and overall health-related quality of
life and intravesical treatment tolerability in people with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

title: Develop Multi-modal Foundation Models for Sepsis Early Detection
text:
Sepsis is a life-threatening condition that leads to widespread inflammation, multiple organ failure, and eventually
death. We will develop accurate, efficient, and interpretable multi-modal foundation models (FMs) for the early
detection of sepsis, which is critical to reducing the risk of death and minimizing the extent of organ damage. Our
FMs, to be pre-trained on a vast dataset of 29 million patient records, will be made accessible to a broader range of
clinicians, enabling them to utilize these models as a basis for swiftly developing specialized in-house tools for the
early detection of sepsis.

title: High-throughput biochemistry with RNA-barcoded proteins
text:
Many variants of human proteins have been identified by sequencing, but the effects of the
amino acid changes are often unknown. Annotation of these effects would be significantly
aided by the results of biochemical activity assays for all the single amino acid variants of a
given protein. We propose to develop a method that covalently links a unique RNA barcode
to each variant, thereby allowing pooled activity assays, with the variants identified simply by
sequencing of their barcodes.

title: The role of conformational dynamics of enveloped virus spike proteins in cell entry
text:
Respiratory viral pathogens, such as SARS-CoV-2 and RSV, can cause deadly infections in human lungs and
have exerted a tremendous public health burden. The proposed program of research focuses on the viral
membrane fusion mechanism of SARS-CoV-2 and RSV, a process that is a prerequisite for a virus to enter host
cells. The proposed studies will employ complementary/synergetic biophysical and biochemical tools to elucidate
molecular mechanisms of the fusion process, guiding the design of future vaccines and therapeutics that target
virus entry.

title: Chemically ligated-guide RNA (lgRNA)-based CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing for elimination of hepatitis B virus cccDNA
text:
Antiviral therapeutics approved by the FDA or currently in clinical trials for treatment of chronic hepatitis B can
efficiently suppress the replication of hepatitis B virus (HBV), reduce viral load and improve liver pathology,
but fail to cure the chronic infection of HBV. This is because those drugs cannot eliminate the most stable
HBV replication intermediate, covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), in the nuclei of hepatocytes, and viral
replication rebounds after discontinuation of treatment. This project addresses the pressing need for the cure
of chronic hepatitis B by elimination and/or permanent inactivation of cccDNA with our proprietary chemically
ligated guide RNA (lgRNA)-based CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing technology.

title: CTCF-dependent mechanisms of ATRX in neuronal differentiation
text:
ATRX is a frequently mutated protein in neurodevelopmental disorders and in several cancers. ATRX has known
function in regulating genome organization. Elucidating its mechanisms and the consequence of ATRX
mutations to genome organization will significantly advance our understanding of ATRX malfunction in disease.

title: Characterizing the Epidemiology of Cannabidiol (CBD) Use Among US adults
text:
I will learn how cannabis (specifically CBD) products have been researched and regulated and
how to apply natural language processing (NLP). I will field a detailed survey with open- and
close-ended questions to (1) Describe the characteristics of CBD users, (2) Characterize CBD
use as a substitute or adjunct to other medications, and (3) Characterize self-reported CBD-
related adverse events. I will apply modern text analysis approaches vested natural language
processing to analyze responses to open-ended questions, discovering responses that cannot
be anticipated based on current understanding or may be missed by theoretical expectations.

title: Mechanisms Underlying Population Differences in Lung Cancer Due to Cigarette Smoking
text: This program brings together highly respected scientists with expertise ranging from epidemiology and biostatistics to molecular aspects of tobacco control to determine why lung cancer risk from cigarette smoking is significantly different among different population groups. The multidisciplinary team in this program follows this important lead to determine new approaches toward prevention of lung cancer, the leading cancer killer in the U.S.
